concepts.def: The right amounts of carbohydrate, protein, lipid, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
Caused by too little or too much of one or more nutrients.
Breaking large insoluble food molecules into small soluble ones.
Caused by a lack of a nutrient, e.g. scurvy from too little vitamin C.
Taking in more energy than is used leads to weight gain.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nutrition & Health — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nutrition & Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nutrition & Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes the innate from the adaptive immune response?
options: Innate is fast, non-specific, and has no memory; adaptive is slower initially, highly specific, and forms memory cells.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Innate immunity attacks viruses and adaptive attacks bacteria.
Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Innate immunity only works in children; adaptive only works in adults.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Subcellular structures”?
options: Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stem cell”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryotic cell”?
options: A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryotic cell”?
options: A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Specialised cells”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
